notes:
Summary: Strandline is building a global low-latency model layer for real-time bidding and personalization. Primary ask: reserved GPU pools across NA and EU with transparent failover headroom and contractual throughput guarantees. Key constraints: aggressive 95th/99th p95 p99 latency targets for model variants, strict EU data residency for user profiles, and cost sensitivity for peak vs baseline traffic.

Highlights from calls: 
- CTO: "We need predictable tail latency under load peaks — not just average throughput. If latency spikes, we lose auctions and revenue."
- Infra lead: preferring H100-class for heavy reranking models, A100 or lower-precision for embedding/serving at scale.
- Security: must support SSO + SCIM; audit logs forwarded to their SIEM; KMS keys per-region.

Technical preferences / constraints: 
- Target throughput: baseline 1,500–2,000 RPS across NA (primary) with burst capacity up to 5k RPS for seasonal traffic.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms and p99 < 220ms for chat/rerank endpoints (end-to-end server-side).
- Reserved GPU planning: want a 20–30% warm failover headroom per-region; cross-region cold failover as contingency for full-zone outages.
- AZ strategy: distribute reserved pools across 3 AZs per region, prefer multi-AZ spread for capacity isolation.
- Failover modes: hot-standby (warm pools prewarmed for key model variants), replica sync for KV caches, and automated routing policy with throttled burst to avoid noisy neighbor spikes.
- Model variants: primary fp16 H100 models for reranking; quantized int8 variants for burst fallback to save cost. Seamless automatic fallback required with degraded-quality signals logged.
- Observability: require token-level cost + latency breakdown per route, 30-day retention for traces, integration with Datadog.

Procurement / SLA negotiation items: 
- Proposed SLA target under discussion: 99.9% uptime for service endpoints, with explicit latency SLO credits for p95/p99 breaches.
- Desired contract: 12–24 month reserved commit with quarterly review windows; want ability to shift reserved capacity between regions with 30d notice.
- Pricing sensitivity: prefer blended committed rate with explicit unit costs for bursts.

POC goals (agreed): 
- Produce a region-by-region reserved GPU sizing spreadsheet (NA primary, EU secondary) with 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive.
- Run Redwood Dedicated benchmark against their reranking model (10k token context, concurrent 200 sessions) and capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization.
- Validate failover time between regions (target RTO < 3 min for routing + cache warmup strategy).

Stated next actions: 
- Redwood to deliver POC sizing & pricing deck (owner: Jordan Lee) by 2025-02-28.
- Strandline infra to provide anonymized sample traffic profile (5 days) and one canonical rerank model container by 2025-02-24.

CRM-style quick notes: 
- Security questionnaire sent 2025-01-31 (SEC-2120).
- Fireflies: call 2025-02-14 detailed SLA discussion (ff-20250214-02b9).
- They asked explicit fallback quantization test cases: Redwood to include quantization bench.

Risks: 
- If cross-region egress costs are high, they may limit cross-region warm pool sizes.
- Legal/data residency could block moving any profile-level processing out of EU region.
- Aggressive p99 targets may require higher reserved capacity or stricter autoscale buffer, increasing committed ARR.
